page.title: Daily fluid intake recommendations for adults
page.text: Adults need fluids every day from drinks and food. Common reference values are about 2.7 liters of total water per day for women and about 3.7 liters for men, including water from food; roughly 20 percent usually comes from food. Needs rise with heat, physical activity, illness, pregnancy and breastfeeding. For most healthy adults thirst is a reliable guide, and pale yellow urine indicates adequate hydration.

page.title: Growing basil indoors: light and watering
page.text: Basil needs at least six hours of bright light a day; a south-facing window or a grow light works best indoors. Water when the top centimeter of soil feels dry and make sure the pot drains well, because soggy roots cause rot. Pinch off flower buds and harvest from the top to keep the plant bushy. Keep it away from cold drafts; basil prefers temperatures above 15 °C.

page.title: Relational vs. document stores
page.text: Relational (SQL) databases store data in tables with a fixed schema and use SQL for queries; they offer strong consistency and joins, which suits transactions and structured data. NoSQL databases include document, key-value, wide-column and graph stores; they use flexible schemas and often scale horizontally across many servers. Many NoSQL systems trade strict consistency for availability and speed. The right choice depends on data shape, query patterns and scaling needs.

page.title: Vienna–Prague timetable and fares
page.text: Direct trains between Vienna and Prague run roughly every two hours, operated by ÖBB, České dráhy and RegioJet. The journey takes about four hours. Saver fares booked in advance start at around 15 to 20 euros, while flexible tickets bought on the day often cost 40 to 60 euros. Trains leave from Wien Hauptbahnhof and arrive at Praha hlavní nádraží. Seat reservations are recommended on weekends.

page.title: Static electricity explained
page.text: Static electricity is a buildup of electric charge on the surface of an object. When two materials rub together, electrons can move from one to the other, leaving one with extra negative charge and the other with a positive charge. Because the charges cannot flow away easily, they stay in place until they find a path, for example when you touch a metal door handle and feel a small spark. Dry air makes static stronger, humid air weakens it.

page.title: Payment reminder templates
page.text: A polite payment reminder should be short, friendly and specific. Start with a neutral subject line such as 'Reminder: invoice #1234 due on 15 March'. In the body, mention the invoice number, amount and due date, assume good faith ('perhaps this slipped through'), attach the invoice again and state how to pay. Close by offering help if there are questions. Send the first reminder a few days after the due date.

page.title: Nutrients to watch on a vegetarian diet
page.text: Vegetarian diets can provide most nutrients, but a few need attention. Vitamin B12 is found almost only in animal products; vegetarians get some from dairy and eggs, but many benefit from fortified foods or supplements. Iron from plants is absorbed less well, which vitamin C can improve. Vitamin D, iodine, zinc and omega-3 fatty acids can also run low, depending on food choices and sun exposure.

page.title: Official castling rules
page.text: Castling moves the king two squares toward a rook and places that rook on the square the king crossed. It is allowed only if neither the king nor that rook has moved before, there are no pieces between them, the king is not in check, and the king does not pass through or land on a square attacked by the opponent. Castling kingside is written 0-0, queenside 0-0-0.
